content: District Health Authorities were administrative divisions within the National Health Service (NHS) in England and Wales, functioning between 1982 and 1996. These authorities operated as a secondary tier of administration beneath the health regions. They replaced the Area Health Authorities, which were generally aligned with non-metropolitan counties, metropolitan boroughs, or groups of London Boroughs, as well as the District Management Teams responsible for the daily operations of hospitals. The two-tier administrative structure had been introduced in 1974. However, during the 1990s, the District Health Authorities underwent several reorganizations and were ultimately abolished in 1996. At that time, single-tier Health Authorities were established, replacing both the District and Regional levels of administration. In the Northern Region, sixteen District Health Authorities were established in 1982, replacing nine Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1992 reduced the number of districts to fourteen. By 1994, the Northern Region was incorporated into the larger Northern and Yorkshire Region, leading to further amalgamations. For instance, North Cumbria District was formed by merging East Cumbria and West Cumbria, South of Tyne District was created from Gateshead and South Tyneside, Tees District was formed by combining Hartlepool, North Tees, and South Tees, and Morecambe Bay District was established from South Cumbria and Lancaster. In the Yorkshire Region, seventeen District Health Authorities were created in 1982, replacing seven Area Health Authorities. Between 1991 and 1993, the number of districts was reduced to seven. In 1994, the Yorkshire Region became part of the Yorkshire and Northern Region. In the Trent Region, twelve District Health Authorities were formed in 1982, replacing eight Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1992 reduced the number of districts to eleven, with the creation of North Nottinghamshire District through the merger of Bassetlaw and Central Nottinghamshire Districts. In 1994, Lincolnshire District was formed by combining North Lincolnshire and South Lincolnshire. In the East Anglia Region, eight District Health Authorities were established in 1982, replacing three Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1992 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to six. In 1994, the East Anglia Region merged with the Oxford Region to form the Anglia and Oxford Region. During this time, East Norfolk District was created by merging Norwich District with part of Great Yarmouth and Waveney District in Norfolk, while Waveney in Suffolk was transferred to Suffolk District. In the North West Thames Region, fourteen District Health Authorities were created in 1982, replacing seven Area Health Authorities. The region's boundaries were adjusted in 1982, with part of the City of Westminster transferred to the North East Thames Region and the Borough of Spelthorne, Surrey, received from the South West Thames Region. Spelthorne returned to the South West Thames Region in 1993. Changes in central London districts occurred in 1985 and 1988. For example, Riverside District was formed in 1985 by merging Hammersmith and Fulham with Victoria Districts, while Parkside District was created in 1988 by merging Paddington & North Kensington with Brent Districts. Parkside District was later abolished in 1993, with parts incorporated into Kensington Chelsea and Westminster, and others into Brent and Harrow. Reorganizations between 1992 and 1994 reduced the number of districts to nine. In the North East Thames Region, fourteen District Health Authorities were formed in 1982, replacing seven Area Health Authorities. In 1990, Bloomsbury and Islington District was created, encompassing the London Borough of Islington and eleven wards from the London Borough of Camden. This district became part of Camden and Islington District in 1993. Reorganizations in 1990 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to seven. In the South East Thames Region, fifteen District Health Authorities were established in 1982, replacing five Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1993 and 1994 reduced the number of districts to eight. In the South West Thames Region, thirteen District Health Authorities were created in 1982, replacing five Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1993 and 1994 reduced the number of districts to ten. In the Wessex Region, ten District Health Authorities were formed in 1982, replacing four Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1994 reduced the number of districts to six. That same year, the Wessex Region merged with the South West Region to form the South and West Region. In the Oxford Region, eight District Health Authorities were created in 1982, replacing four Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1993 reduced the number of districts to four. In 1994, the Oxford Region merged with the East Anglia Region to form the Anglia and Oxford Region. In the South Western Region, eight District Health Authorities were established in 1982, replacing four Area Health Authorities. Reorganizations in 1991 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to five. In 1994, the South West Region merged with the Wessex Region to form the South and West Region. In the West Midlands Region, twenty-two District Health Authorities were created in 1982, replacing eleven Area Health Authorities. For example, North East Warwickshire District merged with South Warwickshire District to form Warwickshire District in 1993. Reorganizations between 1991 and 1993 reduced the number of districts to fifteen. In the Mersey Region, ten District Health Authorities were formed in 1982, replacing six Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1993 reduced the number of districts to seven. In 1994, the Mersey Region merged with the North Western Region to form the North West Region. In the North Western Region, nineteen District Health Authorities were created in 1982, replacing eleven Area Health Authorities. A reorganization in 1994 reduced the number of districts. That same year, the North Western Region merged with the Mersey Region to form the North West Region. In Wales, nine District Health Authorities were established in 1982. Unlike England, Wales did not have Area Health Authorities, as the entire country was under the jurisdiction of the Welsh Office.
